problem: verification-architecture.md line 17 states plainly: 'The judgment column is the AGENT's (right-altitude prompts), never a hardcoded classifier'; the purity boundary map (lines 9-16) puts 'craft writing + V0.5 craft scoring' in the NON-DETERMINISTIC / agent-judgment column, annotated '-- judged by the running model, NOT hardcoded regex --'. Line 25 (PROP-3 row) further states the REQ-5(d) semantic 'no claim of having run' check must be 'a DEFINED binary check, NOT a keyword blocklist'. Yet gates/v05.sh's own header comment (lines 16-19) and body (lines 48-92) show the REAL, non-test-mode implementation of ALL FIVE V0.5 criteria -- including (d), the exact criterion verification-architecture.md singles out -- as hardcoded grep/regex pattern matches (e.g. line 52 'secret|nobody|never|why|mistake|waste|pain' for hook detection; line 70 'i (ran|executed|cloned)|running the (repo|script|tool)|error-log:|stack trace' for the no-run-claim check). This is precisely the anti-pattern the spec explicitly forbids for this exact gate. CRIT-001's passThreshold text is 'PROP-5 test green: stubbed V0 or V0.5 FAIL -> no PUBLISHED sentinel...; only both-PASS writes the sentinel' -- it validates ONLY the publish-gate WIRING using ARTICLE_TEST_FORCE_V05 stub injection (tests/test-prop5-failclosed-publish.sh calls gates/publish-gate.sh directly with forced PASS/FAIL, never exercising the real v05.sh scoring logic). No CRIT in this contract requires that the real (non-stubbed) V0.5 implementation actually honor the judged-not-hardcoded mandate. A Phase 3 code adversary could sign off on this contract's criteria in full while the shipped gate is a keyword-blocklist that the spec's own authors called out as the failure mode to avoid.
fix: Add an explicit passThreshold clause to CRIT-001 (or a new CRIT) requiring that the non-test-mode path of gates/v05.sh delegate criteria (a)-(d) scoring to the running agent's judgment (a right-altitude prompt invoking a fresh-context/adversary-style scoring call), not a static keyword grep -- OR, if Sprint 1 intentionally ships a mechanical approximation as a bootstrap, the contract must say so explicitly and defer the agent-judged version to a named future sprint, exactly as it already does for real publish/earn. Leaving this silent contradicts the spec's own stated design and violates the project's standing 'never hardcode a judgment as regex' rule.
